title: Ex-Meta scientists want to bring visual AI to the factory floor
slides: Ex-Meta scientists claim factory floors are blind, can they see?
Their visual AI spots defects invisible to human eyes.
But it fails on rare, unseen products and needs retraining.
Your factory can test it on one line and measure yield.
Start a pilot now or risk rivals seeing better first.
thread_text:
1. Factory floors are blind.

Ex-Meta scientists say most factories can't see their own defects. Their AI spots what humans miss, but only on known products.

2. The catch: rare items.

Their visual AI fails on unseen products and needs retraining. That's a hidden cost most pilots don't budget for.

3. Test on one line.

You can run a pilot on a single production line and measure yield improvement. Real data beats speculation.

4. The risk of waiting.

Rivals are already exploring this. If you delay, they see defects first—and your yield gap grows.

5. Start a pilot this week.

Pick one line, run their AI for a shift, compare yield. If it doesn't win, you lose only a day. If it does, you're ahead.

Ex-Meta scientists built visual AI that catches defects invisible to the human eye—but only on products it has already seen. Throw it a rare, new item and it breaks, needing expensive retraining.

The play: test it on a single line for one shift, then compare your yield numbers against yesterday. Real data beats a sales pitch. 📊
